neighbours.label: In Python code, the name of a standard-library module whose name is a coined compound rather than an everyday English word (or a dotted sub-module of one), written right before the dot to reach one of its classes or functions inside an assignment or call (x = <module>.<member>(...)); the peak is on the module name. Weak: stdlib modules named by a plain English word (queue, math, socket, random), third-party packages, attributes of ordinary variables (self.client.get), module names inside import lines, and the same names in prose.
neighbours.short: coined stdlib module name before a dot (pathlib., tempfile.)
